name: Maz Repository
observations: GitHub repo Mazoo85/maz
Holds two things: the Maz Engine (native C++ game engine) and ZOMBOID: ANCHORAGE (browser game)
Root README.md documents both projects

name: Maz Engine
observations: Native C++20 + Vulkan + SDL3 game engine
2D-first but architected so 3D drops in later (renderer interface, camera abstraction, scene graph)
Built with CMake >= 3.24, warnings-as-errors; SDL3 and GLM fetched automatically via FetchContent
Current milestone is M0: the walking skeleton (window, fixed-timestep loop, Vulkan clear-screen renderer, clean shutdown)
Degrades gracefully with no GPU/display so it runs headless in CI
Lives under engine/ with core/, platform/, math/, render/ modules
Demo app is apps/sandbox; supports --headless and --frames N flags
Design docs: docs/ROADMAP.md (14-phase plan) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

name: ZOMBOID: ANCHORAGE
observations: Browser-playable Project Zomboid-style open-world zombie survival game
Rendered as a 1990s SEGA 16-bit neon arcade title
Pure HTML5 Canvas + vanilla JavaScript, no build step or dependencies
Map is a 160x140 tile replica of downtown & midtown Anchorage, Alaska with real street and building names
Entry point is index.html; can also run via python3 -m http.server
Is the engine's eventual Phase 13 native-port target and design reference

name: ZOMBOID source layout
observations: index.html: shell + script load order
css/style.css: arcade-cabinet styling, scanlines
js/world.js: Anchorage data (avenues, streets, named buildings)
js/worldgen.js: bakes data into a tile grid + loot containers
js/items.js: item definitions + themed loot tables
js/audio.js: WebAudio chiptune SFX + music
js/game.js: engine (states, input, sim, combat, rendering, HUD)

name: Codebase Memory MCP
observations: MCP server that gives Claude persistent, cross-session memory about this codebase
Configured in .mcp.json as server name codebase-memory
Uses the official @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory package via npx
Launched through scripts/codebase-memory-server.sh, which pins the memory file to an absolute path in the repo
Knowledge graph is stored at .claude/codebase-memory.json and committed to git
Documented in docs/CODEBASE_MEMORY.md

name: Blender to Maz pipeline
observations: Pathway for getting 3D models from Blender into the Maz Engine via the glTF 2.0 standard format
Blender export helper is tools/blender/maz_export.py (works as an add-on: File > Export > 'Maz Engine (.glb)', and headless via blender --background --python)
Export settings: GLB binary, Y-up right-handed, apply modifiers, export normals + UVs
Engine loader is maz::assets::loadModel in engine/src/assets/Model.cpp, header engine/include/maz/assets/Model.hpp
Uses vendored cgltf single-header parser at engine/third_party/cgltf, compiled as its own maz_cgltf target with relaxed warnings (engine builds first-party code with -Werror)
Vertex is POD (position[3], normal[3], uv[2]) so a mesh can be uploaded to a Vulkan vertex buffer verbatim later
sandbox gained --load-model PATH flag to load a glTF/GLB and log stats headless
Test asset assets/models/cube.gltf (24 verts, 12 tris, embedded buffer); ctest model_load_gltf verifies it
Loads geometry only for now; drawing models on screen needs the Phase 3 mesh renderer
Documented in docs/BLENDER_PIPELINE.md

name: Maz Engine 3D rendering
observations: Effort to draw 3D models (e.g. Blender-imported meshes) on screen; roadmap Phase 3

maz::scene::Camera (engine/include/maz/scene/Camera.hpp, src/scene/Camera.cpp): perspective camera producing Vulkan-correct view + projection matrices (right-handed, depth 0..1, Y-flip via maz::math::perspective)
Camera is unit-tested by tests/unit_camera.cpp (maz_unit_tests / ctest unit_camera): checks screen-center projection, Vulkan Y-flip, 0..1 depth ordering; runs with no GPU
Next step is the Vulkan mesh renderer: VMA buffers, graphics pipeline, depth buffer, MVP push constants, mesh.vert/frag shaders, indexed draw of maz::assets::Model
The dev/cloud sandbox has NO Vulkan SDK, no shader compiler, no GPU/display — engine GPU code cannot be compiled or run there; it is verified via GitHub Actions CI instead

DONE (CI-compile-verified): Vulkan mesh renderer landed. maz::render::MeshRenderer (engine/src/render/MeshRenderer.{hpp,cpp}) builds a graphics pipeline (vertex layout matching assets::Vertex, VERTEX-stage push constants = mvp+model mat4s = 128 bytes, dynamic viewport/scissor, depth test LESS, cull NONE) and per-mesh host-visible vertex/index buffers; loads SPIR-V shaders from beside the executable via SDL_GetBasePath
Depth buffer added to VulkanSwapchain (D32_SFLOAT image/view/memory; render pass + framebuffers have color+depth; both cleared each frame) for correct 3D occlusion
VulkanContext::findMemoryType added, shared by depth image and mesh buffers
Renderer interface gained uploadModel(model)->bool and drawModel(mvp, model); VulkanRenderer owns a MeshRenderer and records mesh draws between beginFrame/endFrame
Shaders engine/shaders/mesh.vert (MVP transform + world-space normal via mat3(model)) and mesh.frag (directional + ambient shading)

sandbox --load-model now uploads to GPU and draws the model as a spinning mesh via maz::scene::Camera (pos 0,1.4,3 look at origin), aspect tracks drawable size; headless no-ops the draw so CI/tests still pass

Verified by GitHub Actions CI run #4 (green): compiles under -Werror on real Vulkan headers, glslang validates the shaders. The actual on-screen spinning cube needs a real GPU (CI has no ICD/surface so the renderer stays inactive there)

Still TODO to see it: user runs ./build/bin/sandbox --load-model assets/models/cube.gltf on a machine with a GPU + display. Future rigor: offscreen render-to-image + pixel readback test (needs lavapipe) to verify pixels headlessly in CI

name: Maz CI
observations: GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml
Runs on push to any branch and on pull_request
Installs Vulkan SDK (libvulkan-dev), glslang-tools, and SDL3 build deps on ubuntu-latest, then cmake configure + build under -Werror + ctest headless (SDL dummy drivers)
Exists because the dev sandbox lacks Vulkan/GPU, so CI is the verification vehicle for engine/GPU code

name: Maz Editor
observations: The visual editor for the Maz Engine; roadmap Phase 12, built in stages. Documented in docs/EDITOR.md
Stage 1 DONE (headless-unit-tested): scene backbone. maz::scene::Scene / Entity / Transform in engine/include/maz/scene/Scene.hpp + src/scene/Scene.cpp
Transform = position + rotationEuler (degrees, applied Y then X then Z) + scale; matrix() composes T*R*S
Scenes save/load to a line-oriented .mazscene text format via maz::scene::saveScene/loadScene; supports quoted strings with \" and \\ escapes; first line is 'maz-scene <version>'
Round-trip verified by tests/unit_scene.cpp (ctest unit_scene) and scene_load_headless ctest (sandbox --headless --scene) — all pure-CPU / headless

MeshRenderer changed to hold MULTIPLE uploaded models: uploadModel returns an int handle (>=0) or -1; draw(handle, mvp, model, extent); Renderer interface now int uploadModel(model) and drawModel(handle, mvp, model)

sandbox gained --scene PATH: loads a .mazscene, uploads each unique model once (dedup by path), draws all entities at their transforms with an orbiting camera; --load-model is now a one-entity spinning scene
Sample scene assets/scenes/demo.mazscene (5 cubes: ground slab, center, towers, floating)

Stage 2 TODO: the actual editor window — Dear ImGui Hierarchy + Inspector panels, live 3D viewport (offscreen render into an ImGui image), transform gizmos. Will be compile-verified in CI, seen on a real GPU
